properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: hash.js@1.1.3 is a real transitive dependency in the shipped node_modules tree (via the ethereumjs/web3 browser-stdlib chain) and provides SHA-1 plus the SHA-2 family. Changeable here by bumping/trimning the dependency tree. No first-party hash.js import found in src — presence is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA is the backbone of this Ethereum toolchain: packages secp256k1@^4.0.1, @types/secp256k1 and @noble/secp256k1@~1.7.0/1.7.1 appear throughout the lockfile as dependencies of ethers v5/v6, ethereumjs-tx and web3. The repo is a Frax smart-contract dev environment; secp256k1 is also used live in first-party Solidity via the ecrecover precompile (separate findings reported). Curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol — migration to ML-DSA is a chain-level decision, not changeable in this

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf@^1.0.0 — the OpenBSD bcrypt-based PBKDF used for SSH/JWT key derivation, not the bcrypt password hash itself. It is a transitive dependency of sshpk (http-signature chain pulled in via web3/maticjs HTTP-stack deps) and pairs with its own vendored tweetnacl. Shipped in node_modules; no first-party use in src. Quantum-relevant only as a KDF (Grover halves its work factor); low priority.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test scaffolding: Math.random() picks random values/indices in BAMM fuzz-test helpers. Genuine non-cryptographic PRNG use, but no secret, key, or security decision depends on the output — kept as the honest record of weak randomness with that caveat.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency evp_bytestokey@^1.0.3 pinned 4x in package-lock.json as part of the browser-crypto shim chain under the ethers v5 toolchain. No first-party call site in this repo — dependency inventory; the single-round MD5 KDF ships in the graph regardless of use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA capability via @noble/curves@1.1.0, declared in the lockfile. No direct first-party call site — the repo signs through ethers v5, which reaches secp256k1 via its own dependency chain. Available in the shipped library is the inventory fact.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 1.0.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 7 sites are live HTTPS client calls (data fetches in the public-scripts checkpointers and proof collector, fraxswap test utils, axios in src/misc/utilities.ts:90) on Node's default TLS config — no cipher/group pinning anywhere. Weakest permitted group x25519; PQ hybrid (X25519MLKEM768) only from Node 24.5+ and the runtime version is unpinned in the tree. Sessions are harvest-now-decrypt-later; changeable here by pinning groups or pinning the Node runtime.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 available in the shipped @noble/curves@1.1.0 (2 lockfile pins). No first-party call site found in the application; presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.1.0 ships the P-256 (secp256r1) implementation alongside secp256k1/ed25519/x25519; pulled in via the ethers v6 dependency chain. Available in the shipped node_modules; no first-party P-256 call site found in src (this repo's chain work is secp256k1). Library facet of this package is inventoried separately as LIB-e9aa10c7.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 — transitive dependency (via ethereumjs-util/web3 browser polyfills) that ships ECDH and ECDSA implementations for secp256k1, P-256, ed25519 and others. Available in the shipped node_modules tree; no first-party ECDH call site found in src JS/TS. Classic ECDH — Shor-vulnerable if ever exercised.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 available via tweetnacl@0.14.5 in the shipped dependency graph. No first-party call site found; presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (the EVM SHA-3 variant) in real use: ~100 lockfile pins for @ethersproject/keccak256@5.7.0 / keccak@^3.0.x, plus live call sites — EIP-712 domain separators and permit typehashes (src/hardhat/test/Fraxswap/utilities.js, src/hardhat/test/old_tests/openzeppelin/signatures.ts), CREATE2 init-code hashes and pair-address derivation, double-hashed storage slots in the l1veFXS proof collector (l1veFXS_proof_collector.js:255), and state-root hashing in Fraxferry/Fraxoracle tests. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 87 lockfile pins: @ethersproject/pbkdf2@5.7.0, pbkdf2@^3.0.17, @types/pbkdf2@^3.0.0 — the browser-crypto shim chain under the ethers v5 toolchain. No first-party PBKDF2 call site; iteration counts and salt parameters are not expressible in a version pin. Dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@^3.0.0 / 2.0.4 / 3.0.1 declared 53 times across the lockfile — scrypt is the memory-hard KDF the ethers/web3 keystore (encrypted JSON wallet) paths use. The build ships scrypt. No first-party keystore decryption found in src (grep for fromEncryptedJson/decryptKeystore: 0 hits), so no first-party call site — presence is what this entry records. scrypt itself is quantum-resistant in practice (Grover square-root only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.3.1 pulled in via ethers v6; ships SHA-256/SHA-3/keccak/ripemd in the node_modules tree. No first-party @noble/hashes import found in src — first-party JS hashes through ethers' own keccak wrappers (covered by the SHA-3 inventory object). Dependency-inventory entry; presence records what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 available via @noble/hashes@1.3.1 in the shipped dependency graph. No first-party call site found; presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/Keccak capability via @noble/hashes@1.3.1 — same algorithm family as the ethers keccak256 object (ALG-052c24b2) but a different library surface; kept separate so the provider attribution survives. No direct first-party call site; the repo's keccak use flows through @ethersproject/keccak256.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 (tweetnacl secretbox) available via tweetnacl@0.14.5. Symmetric authenticated encryption, quantum-safe; no first-party call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is present in the lockfile as a dependency of sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf (the http-signature SSH/JWT key-parsing chain under web3/maticjs HTTP deps) and carries its own vendored copy inside bcrypt-pbkdf. It ships Ed25519 signatures, X25519 ECDH, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE and SHA-512 — all quantum-vulnerable primitives available to the shipped tree. Per-algorithm facets are inventoried as separate objects (Ed25519 ALG-683d5cd2, X25519 ALG-defedad1, XSalsa20-Poly1305 ALG-f58a8f00 — scout 1's shard).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes declared in the dependency graph — supplies SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE/HKDF/keccak surfaces to the Ethereum toolchain. Dependency inventory; no direct first-party import found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves — the elliptic-curve library of the ethers v6 dependency chain; ships secp256k1, P-256, ed25519, x25519 and other curves in node_modules. P-256 algorithm facet inventoried as ALG-a6da3577. No first-party @noble/curves import found in src; scripts reach it indirectly through ethers' signing-key/wallet wrappers. Availability is what this entry records for the shipped image.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The npm `https` package is a DIRECT dependency (package.json:57, "https": "^1.0.0") — a thin wrapper around Node's built-in https module. Every request through it opens a Node TLS session on that runtime's default settings: non-PQ key exchange (X25519/ECDHE), harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed wherever the scripts fetch over TLS.
